Plot the standard normal curve with score scales

Source: R/standard_normal_scales.R
standard_normal_scales.Rd

Draws the standard normal curve, divided at every standard deviation and marked with the percentage of cases in each interval, with the z, T, cumulative percentage, percentile, sten, stanine, grade and IQ scales lined up under it, so that a score on one scale can be read off on the others. In blues, reds or greens, colour shows how common a score is; the diverging palette colours the bands blue below the mean and red above it. Each palette has a light and a dark mode.

Usage

standard_normal_scales(
  size = 3,
  palette = c("blues", "reds", "greens", "diverging"),
  mode = c("light", "dark")
)

Arguments

size

Text size of all labels, in millimetres (ggplot2 text size). The default of 3 suits figures around 7 inches wide; about 5 suits figures around 12 inches wide.

palette

The colours of the chart:

"blues", "reds" or "greens"

One colour, which shows how common a score is: under the curve, the intervals that hold more cases are darker, so 34.13% is the darkest and 0.13% the lightest, and the bands are darker the nearer the mean they are.

"diverging"

A neutral gray under the curve, and bands blue below the mean and red above it, darker the further from the mean, with gray for a band centred on the mean.

mode

"light" for dark text on a white background, or "dark" for light text on a near-black background. In the dark mode the colours that are darker in the light mode are brighter instead, so that they still stand out from the background.

Value

A ggplot object. Print it to draw the chart, or save it with ggplot2::ggsave(). The chart keeps a fixed aspect ratio and is about 2.2 times as wide as it is tall, so a figure with those proportions, such as 7 by 3.2 inches, has no empty margins.

Details

All scales are placed on the z axis:

  • z: standard score, mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

  • T: \(50 + 10z\).

  • Cumulative %: the percentage of cases below each standard deviation, from \(z = -3\) to \(z = 3\): 0.1, 2.3, 15.9, 50, 84.1, 97.7 and 99.9.

  • Percentile: the z values of the 1st, 5th, 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th, 90th, 95th and 99th percentiles.

  • Sten: ten bands half a standard deviation wide, sten 1 below \(z = -2\) and sten 10 above \(z = 2\) (mean 5.5, standard deviation 2).

  • Stanine: nine bands half a standard deviation wide, stanine 5 from \(z = -0.25\) to \(z = 0.25\) (mean 5, standard deviation 2).

  • Grade: groups of stanines, E (1-2), D (3), C (4-6), B (7) and A (8-9).

  • IQ: \(100 + 15z\).

The chart is standard_normal_custom drawn with standard_normal_scales_data(): start from those to change the scales.

See also

standard_normal_custom, standard_normal_scales_data

Examples

standard_normal_scales()

standard_normal_scales(palette="reds")

standard_normal_scales(palette="diverging",mode="dark")

standard_normal_scales(size=5)

# save it with the chart's proportions
ggsave(file.path(tempdir(),"standard_normal_scales.png"),standard_normal_scales(),
       width=7,height=3.2)
